Treat capacity arithmetic as an estimate until synchronized telemetry confirms it. Reproduce in staging and temporarily enforce conservative token-based admission (queue or reject) plus a context limit.

Falsifiable hypothesis H1 for variant 109: live per-request KV-cache growth, potentially amplified by allocator fragmentation, exhausts usable device headroom. At admission, each decode step, completion, and OOM, correlate request IDs with KV bytes/tokens, active sequences, allocated and reserved bytes, largest free block, free headroom, prefill workspace, activation and communication buffers, and host/pinned usage. Stratify by prompt length, generated length, batch, and concurrency. Support H1 only when matched strata show OOM probability increasing with live KV/active sequences and falling headroom or a large reserved-minus-allocated gap; falsify it when KV is bounded and another pool tracks the failure.

Controlled experiment: in staging, randomize request traces into matched strata and vary one factor at a time (concurrency, prompt/output budget, batch, max context, cache mode, precision) while holding model, hardware, software, and traffic mix fixed. Repeat enough times to estimate OOM and rejection rates with confidence intervals, and collect correctness, TTFT/TPOT, throughput, P99 latency, allocator/KV reclamation, and thermal/resource telemetry. Compare paged KV/prefix caching, quantization, and context limits only behind correctness and tail-latency gates. Roll back a canary on any unexplained correctness regression, safety/isolation issue, OOM increase, or predefined latency/error SLO breach; retain admission control until evidence supports a larger budget.

Paging, prefix sharing, quantization, offload, and admission changes can affect correctness, isolation, bandwidth, and tail latency.
evidence_required: Confirm device-versus-host OOM attribution and byte units with synchronized runtime, allocator, and hardware telemetry.
Run randomized matched replay on target model, engine, and hardware with predefined OOM, correctness, latency, throughput, and rejection gates.
